summary: Case-insensitive username normalization causes intermittent model-hub login failures behind service-proxy
description:
Issue summary:
Several internal engineers report login failures when accessing model-hub via the internal runner UI behind the service-mesh proxy. Failures appear intermittent and correlate with users who have Okta primaryEmail values containing mixed case or recently-added alternate emails.

Impact:
- ~12 engineers in ML infra and platform teams unable to open model-hub sessions intermittently.
- Blocking workflows that require quick model inspection and debug on Dedicated clusters.

Environment:
- prod environment, us-east region.
- Affected routes: /auth/session, /runner/login -> proxied through service-mesh sidecar to identity-proxy.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Okta user has primaryEmail or alternateEmail with mixed-case (e.g., Dev.Example@ExampleCorp.com) or recently added alias.
2. User initiates login via console -> redirect to Okta -> successful auth.
3. Callback to identity-proxy includes user principal name in header X-Remote-User with original casing.
4. Service-mesh or auth-service normalizes headers differently depending on path; sometimes username is lowercased, other times preserved.
5. model-hub session creation fails with 403 session binding mismatch.

Observed behavior:
- 403 from auth-service on session create: "session-user-mismatch" logs.
- identity-proxy logs show principal=Dev.Example@ExampleCorp.com, auth-service shows principal=dev.example@examplecorp.com for same request trace id.
- Users can retry and sometimes succeed; other times require clearing browser cookies or using incognito.

Expected behavior:
- Username normalization should be consistent across proxy and downstream services. Case normalization should be agreed and documented; session binding should accept canonicalized forms.

Temporary workaround:
- Support applied a run-time rule in service-mesh to preserve original header casing for X-Remote-User on /runner/login for affected services (mitigates ~80% of occurrences).
- Affected users instructed to empty cookies and retry if they see 403.
steps_to_reproduce: User with mixed-case Okta email authenticates via console
Callback to identity-proxy sends X-Remote-User header
Service-mesh or auth-service normalizes casing inconsistently
comments: 2026-03-11T15:05 Priya Nair: Initial report from ML infra team. Attached one user trace and screenshots. Marking P1 due to blocking debugging workflows.
2026-03-11T16:12 Liam Chen: Reproduced locally behind staging mesh. Observed header casing difference between sidecar and identity-proxy. Spun up packet capture and added trace ids to logs.
2026-03-12T09:40 Maria Gonzalez (SRE): Applied temporary mTLS route rule to preserve X-Remote-User on runner path. Monitoring for recurrence. Noted similar past incident notes in INT-314159.
2026-03-12T11:02 Dev Tools (comment): We saw a near-identical failure during last proxy upgrade; opened PR to add canonicalization helper in identity-proxy. PR link posted in related_github_prs.

2026-03-13T08:21 Liam Chen: Collected sample Okta profiles (anonymized) showing mixed-case aliases. Working on patch to normalize to lowercase at identity-proxy boundary and include canonical_username header for downstream verification.

2026-03-13T14:55 SRE oncall: Service-mesh rule remains; frequency of incidents dropped from ~6/day to ~1/day for the past 24h. Will delay full rollout until code review lands and QA completes in staging.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: Inconsistent header casing normalization between service-mesh sidecar (Envoy config) and identity-proxy produces two different username tokens for same auth flow. Downstream auth-service binds sessions to canonicalized username (lowercased), but model-hub sometimes receives original-cased header leading to mismatch. Evidence: correlated trace ids show principal casing divergence. Temporary mitigation: preserve header casing at mesh layer. Root fix: canonicalize at identity-proxy and add canonical_username claim to JWT issued to internal services. Also add validation to auth-service to accept both forms while rollout occurs.
resolution: Partial mitigation applied (service-mesh header preservation) which reduced occurrences. Planned next steps: (1) land identity-proxy PR to canonicalize usernames and emit canonical_username in JWT (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/identity-proxy/pull/842), (2) patch auth-service to accept canonical_username as authoritative for session binding (PR staged), (3) QA in staging with synthetic cases, (4) gradual rollout with feature flag and monitor. No full resolution yet; target for completion: 2026-03-20.
